facts.text: Middleburg was founded in 1787 by Revolutionary War officer Leven Powell, who bought the land for just $2.50 an acre from Joseph Chinn.
The town’s name evolved from Chinn’s Crossroads to Powell Town, and finally to Middleburg, reflecting its position midway between Alexandria and Winchester.
The Red Fox Inn & Tavern, opened in 1728 as Chinn’s Ordinary, claims to be the oldest continually operated inn in the United States.
The town’s historic downtown, listed on the National Register of Historic Places, preserves a 19th‑century core that attracts visitors year‑round.
Middleburg hosts the National Sporting Library, a 15,000‑square‑foot research center that publishes the online Thoroughbred Heritage archive.
